chunks: “Judges are four: three are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. A man who judges with injustice while he knows is in the Fire. A man who judges with injustice while he does not know is in the Fire. A man who judges with truth while he does not know is in the Fire. And a man who judges with the truth while he knows is in Paradise.”

And he عليه السلام said: “Judgment is of two kinds: the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the judgment of the people of Jahiliyyah. So whoever misses the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has judged by the judgment of the people of Jahiliyyah. And whoever judges for two dirhams by other than what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has sent down has indeed committed kufr in Allah, the Exalted.”

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: the state or way of pre-Islamic ignorance opposed to divine guidance
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: judgment or ruling in legal and authoritative matters
key_terms.الْقُضَاةُ: judges; those who issue legal rulings between people
key_terms.بِالْحَقِّ: with the truth; in accordance with what is right
key_terms.بِجَوْرٍ: with injustice; by an oppressive or wrongful judgment
key_terms.كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ: committed kufr in Allah; a grave rejection by ruling against divine revelation
key_terms.مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: what Allah has sent down; divine revelation as the basis of judgment

ai.seo_question: Which judges are condemned in the Fire, and what does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about ruling without Allah’s judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith divides judges into four categories and teaches that only the one who judges with truth on the basis of knowledge attains Paradise. It condemns ruling without knowledge or contrary to what Allah عزّ وجلّ has revealed, and contrasts divine judgment with the judgment of Jahiliyyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3221 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The judges are four: three are in the Fire, and one is in Paradise.
A man who judges unjustly while he knows is in the Fire.
A man who judges unjustly while he does not know is in the Fire.
A man who judges justly while he does not know is in the Fire.
And a man who judges justly while he knows is in Paradise."

Al-Sadiq (as) also said:
"Judgment is of two kinds: the judgment of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and the judgment of the people of ignorance.
Whoever deviates from the judgment of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has judged by the judgment of the people of ignorance.
And whoever judges for two dirhams contrary to what Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed has indeed disbelieved in Allah (swt), the Exalted."
